entities.type_justification: Courthouse represents a judicial body's physical location, aligning with 'Court' as the entity where legal cases are adjudicated.
The general Organization class fits structured groups like 'Suno AI', 'GEMA', and 'OpenAI' which are all legal entities with specific purposes.
Names like 'Tobias Holzmueller' and 'Kristina Bach' clearly represent individual humans, matching the Person class definition.

nary_nodes.label: Munich Regional Court Rules Suno AI Violated Copyrights
evidence: The Munich Regional Court ruled on Friday that Suno AI, a US-based company, which generates songs from text prompts. has violated copyrights and has to disclose illicit revenues.
According to the verdict, Suno will have to pay damages that have yet to be quantified. Suno has disagreed with the ruling and said it would evaluate all available options, including an appeal.
nary_nodes.type_definition: A legal ruling where a court determines a copyright violation has occurred.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org class captures a court's decision on copyright infringement; the new type is a specific legal event under Event.

The Munich Regional Court ruled on Friday that Suno AI, a US-based company, which generates songs from text prompts. has violated copyrights and has to disclose illicit revenues.
The lawsuit initiated in January 2025 by GEMA, Germany's state-mandated licensing agency, argued that Suno trained its AI models on copyrighted music without obtaining licences or compensating its rights holders.

According to the verdict, Suno will have to pay damages that have yet to be quantified. Suno has disagreed with the ruling and said it would evaluate all available options, including an appeal.
"This is a verdict of global significance," Gema CEO Tobias Holzmueller told Reuters.

nary_nodes.label: GEMA CEO States Verdict Has Global Significance
evidence: "This is a verdict of global significance," Gema CEO Tobias Holzmueller told Reuters.

"This is a verdict of global significance," Gema CEO Tobias Holzmueller told Reuters.
The lawsuit has been closely watched, as it is one of the first major cases anywhere in the world to test how traditional copyright law applies to AI music training and AI-generated music outputs.

nary_nodes.label: Suno Argues Against Jurisdiction of German Court
evidence: Among Suno's arguments was the fact that the German court does not have proper jurisdiction to rule on AI model training activities that occurred exclusively inside the United States.

evidence_resolved.quote: Among Suno's arguments was the fact that the German court does not have proper jurisdiction to rule on AI model training activities that occurred exclusively inside the United States.

evidence_resolved.sentence:
Among Suno's arguments was the fact that the German court does not have proper jurisdiction to rule on AI model training activities that occurred exclusively inside the United States.
The proceedings could help determine whether AI music companies must obtain licenses before training their models on copyrighted songs, and whether AI-generated music that closely resembles existing songs constitutes copyright infringement.
